- [passage] - If the element is an object, the index descends into the object to traverse and index its contents. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/reference/embedded-object-behavior.md#wildcard-indexes-on-arrays · keywords: index, wildcard index
- [passage] - If the element is a primitive value, the index records that value. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/reference/embedded-object-behavior.md#wildcard-indexes-on-arrays · keywords: index, wildcard index
- [passage] If a field is a nested document or array, the wildcard index recurses into the document/array and indexes all scalar fields in the document/array. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes/ · keywords: index, wildcard index · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndexes.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes.md
- [passage] - If the field is an object, the wildcard index descends into the object and indexes its contents. The wildcard index continues descending into any additional embedded documents it encounters. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/reference/embedded-object-behavior.md · keywords: index, wildcard index
- [passage] - If the element is an object, the wildcard index descends into the object to index its contents. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/reference/embedded-object-behavior.md · keywords: index, wildcard index
- [passage] - If the element is an array (that is, an array which is embedded directly within the parent array), the wildcard index does not traverse the embedded array, but indexes the *entire* array as a single value. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/reference/embedded-object-behavior.md · keywords: index, wildcard index
- [passage] The document is not indexed if all of the fields in the compound wildcard index are missing. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/index-wildcard-compound.md#general-considerations-for-wildcard-indexes · keywords: index, wildcard index
- [passage] If a field is an embedded document or array (like `attributes.size`), the wildcard index recurses into the field and indexes all embedded scalar field values. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/create-wildcard-index-multiple-fields.md#results · keywords: index, wildcard index, attributes.size
- [fact] Fitting hot indexes and the working set in RAM is a performance recommendation, not a strict requirement for most storage engines; MongoDB staff said the docs' 'must' should read 'should'. The In-Memory Storage Engine (Enterprise) does require all data to fit in inMemorySizeGB. — https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/working-set-must-fit-in-memory/3287 · keywords: index, index overhead, Index Storage and RAM Fit and Write-Path Overhead
- [passage] Rolling index builds are an alternative to [default index builds.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#std-label-index-operations) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/build-indexes-on-sharded-clusters.md#about-this-task · keywords: index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/build-indexes-on-replica-sets.md
- [passage] Make sure you are not performing [DDL operations](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/ddl-operations.md#std-label-ddl-operations) while conducting the rolling index build. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/build-indexes-on-sharded-clusters.md#considerations · keywords: index, index build
- [passage] An index build is not stopped if there is insufficient available disk space. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: index, index build
- [passage] If there are any key constraint violations, the index build fails. The primary aborts the index build and creates an associated "abortIndexBuild" oplog entry. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md
- [passage] Hidden indexes are not used to support queries. If you hide an index and observe substantial negative performance impact, consider keeping and unhiding the index so queries can resume using it. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-indexes.md#remove-indexes · keywords: hidden index, index
- [passage] Additionally, if there is a collation on the index key, you can only ensure uniqueness if the collation is simple. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique.md#sharded-clusters-and-unique-indexes · keywords: index, unique index
- [passage] If the `_id` field is not the shard key, the uniqueness constraint only applies to the shard that stores the document. This means that two or more documents can have the same `_id` value, provided they occur on different shards. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique.md#sharded-clusters-and-unique-indexes · keywords: index, unique index, _id
- [passage] In cases where the `_id` field is not the shard key, MongoDB expects applications to ensure the uniqueness of `_id` values across the shards, for example, by using a unique identifier to populate the `_id` field. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique.md#sharded-clusters-and-unique-indexes · keywords: index, unique index, _id

## Structure and components

- [passage] For a sharded collection distributed across multiple shards, one or more shards may contain a chunk with duplicate documents. As such, the create index operation may succeed on some of the shards (that is, the ones without duplicates) but not on others (that is, the ones with duplicates). To avoid leaving inconsistent indexes across shards, you can issue the [`db.collection.dropIndex()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropindex.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.dropIndex) from a [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) to drop the index from the collection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#sharded-collections · keywords: dropIndex, index, index build, db.collection.dropIndex(), mongos
- [passage] You can create a text index that contains every document field with string data in a collection. These text indexes are called **wildcard text indexes**. Wildcard text indexes support [`$text`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/text.md#mongodb-query-op.-text) [queries](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/text-search/on-prem.md#std-label-text-search-on-prem) on unknown, arbitrary, or dynamically generated fields. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text/create-wildcard-text-index.md · keywords: index, text index, wildcard index, $text
- [passage] Only use wildcard text indexes when the fields you want to index are unknown or may change. Wildcard text indexes don't perform as well as targeted text indexes on specific fields. If your collection contains arbitrary field names that prevent targeted indexes, consider remodeling your schema to have consistent field names. To learn more about targeted indexes, see [Create Indexes to Support Your Queries.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/data-modeling/schema-design-process/create-indexes.md#std-label-create-indexes-to-support-queries) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text/create-wildcard-text-index.md#about-this-task · keywords: index, text index, wildcard index · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/create-wildcard-index-single-field.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/create-wildcard-index-all-fields.md
- [passage] - You can include a wildcard text index as part of a compound text index. If the field path contains more than 8 explicit indices, to fulfill the query, MongoDB either: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/reference/embedded-object-behavior.md#array-index-limitation · keywords: index, wildcard index
- [passage] - Wildcard indexes are [sparse](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md#std-label-index-type-sparse). They only include entries for documents that contain the indexed field. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/index-wildcard-compound.md#general-considerations-for-wildcard-indexes · keywords: index, wildcard index · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard.md

For example, if you have a collection that contains a field that is never queried, you can omit that field from the index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/create-wildcard-index-multiple-fields.md · keywords: index, wildcard index

- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 5.0, the `wildcardProjection` option for [wildcard indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard.md#std-label-wildcard-index-core) is included in the [index signature](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-index-signature). This means that you can create multiple wildcard indexes with the same [key pattern](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createindexes.md#std-label-key_patterns) as long as the `wildcardProjection` options do not contain the same fields. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/reference/wildcard-projection-signature.md · keywords: index, wildcard index, wildcardProjection
- [passage] Only use wildcard indexes when the fields you want to index are unknown or may change. Wildcard indexes don't perform as well as targeted indexes on specific fields. To learn more about targeted indexes, see Create Indexes to Support Your Queries. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-wildcard/ · keywords: index, wildcard index
- [passage] Wildcard indexes are sparse indexes and only contain entries for documents that have the indexed field, even if the index field contains a null value. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-wildcard/ · keywords: index, wildcard index
- [passage] Wildcard indexes have specific behavior when the indexed field contains an embedded object (for example, `attributes.secret_feature`). For more information, see [Wildcard Indexes on Embedded Objects and Arrays.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/reference/embedded-object-behavior.md#std-label-wildcard-index-embedded-object-behavior) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/create-wildcard-index-single-field.md#results · keywords: index, wildcard index, attributes.secret_feature
- [passage] This index supports single-field queries on any field in the collection. If a document contains an embedded document or array, the wildcard index traverses the document or array and stores the value for all fields in the document or array. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/create-wildcard-index-all-fields.md#results · keywords: index, wildcard index
- [fact] A compound wildcard index may contain only one wildcard term (e.g. { userID: 1, "object1.$**": 1, "object2.$**": 1 } is rejected), and its non-wildcard terms must be single-key; multikey (array) terms are not allowed. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/upcoming/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/reference/restrictions/ · keywords: index, wildcard index, Wildcard and Compound Wildcard Indexes
- [passage] Optional. A flag that determines whether the index is hidden from the query planner. A hidden index is not evaluated as part of query plan selection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes/ · keywords: hidden index, index

- [passage] Queryable Encryption always outputs a different encrypted value, even for the same input. The server considers each encrypted value unique, even though the decrypted value may not be. This means that even if a collection uses an index-enforced unique constraint on fields, the collection can still contain multiple documents with duplicate plaintext values for that field. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/reference/limitations.md#unique-indexes · keywords: index, unique index
- [passage] If you drop an index that is actively used in production, your application may incur a performance degradation. To ensure queries can still use an index during modification, you can create a temporary, redundant index that contains the same fields as the modified index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-indexes.md#minimize-performance-impact-with-a-temporary-index · keywords: mongodb-special-indexes-and-index-builds

## How it works

- [passage] In previous releases, when the primary committed the index build, the write concern specified how many nodes must finish the index build before the command returned success. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setindexcommitquorum/ · keywords: index, index build, commit quorum · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md
- [passage] The [primary](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-primary) marks index build as ready only after a simple majority of data-bearing voting members "vote" to commit the index build. For more information on index builds and the voting process, see [Index Builds in Replicated Environments.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#std-label-index-operations-replicated-build) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndexes.md#create-indexes-with-commit-quorum · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndex.md
- [fact] On replica sets and sharded clusters with featureCompatibilityVersion 4.4+, a build runs simultaneously on all data-bearing members (on sharded clusters only on shards holding the collection). The primary writes startIndexBuild, members vote when done scanning, and the primary writes commitIndexBuild after a commit quorum (default votingMembers) votes and no constraint violation is found; otherwise abortIndexBuild. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build, Index Build Strategies
- [passage] You can resume some interrupted index builds when the commit quorum is set to the default "votingMembers". — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setindexcommitquorum/ · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes/
- [passage] Index creation is a multistage process. The index creation process uses the commit quorum to minimize replication lag on secondary nodes. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setindexcommitquorum/ · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build
- [passage] Changed in version 8.0: The commit quorum specifies how many nodes must be ready to finish the index build before the primary commits the index build. In contrast, when the primary has committed the index build, the write concern specifies how many nodes must replicate the index build oplog entry before the command returns success. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setindexcommitquorum/ · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md
- [passage] If a primary or secondary mongod performs a clean shutdown with "force" : true or receives a SIGTERM signal during an index build, and the commitQuorum is set to the default votingMembers, the index build progress is saved to disk. The mongod automatically recovers the index build when restarted and continues from the saved checkpoint. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md
- [passage] If the mongod is the primary, it waits until it has a commit quorum of votes (all voting data-bearing members by default) before continuing the index build process. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build
- [passage] Index creation is a [multistage process](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#std-label-index-build-process). The index creation process uses the `commit quorum` to minimize replication lag on secondary nodes. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setIndexCommitQuorum.md#behavior · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build
- [passage] 5. When the primary has a quorum of votes, it checks for any key constraint violations such as duplicate key errors. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#index-builds-in-replicated-environments · keywords: index, index build, unique index
- [passage] - [Unique indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique.md#std-label-index-type-unique) Wildcard indexes are [sparse](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md#std-label-index-type-sparse) indexes. They do not support queries when an indexed field does not exist. A wildcard index will index the document if the wildcard field has a `null` value. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes.md#wildcard-indexes · keywords: index, unique index, wildcard index, null
- [passage] After you create a wildcard text index, when you insert or update documents, the index updates to include any new string field values. As a result, wildcard text indexes negatively impact performance for inserts and updates. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text/create-wildcard-text-index.md#about-this-task · keywords: index, text index, wildcard index
- [passage] For replica sets, run [`db.collection.dropIndex()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropindex.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.dropIndex) on the [primary](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-primary). The primary stops the index build and creates an associated "abortIndexBuild" [oplog](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-oplog) entry. Secondaries which replicate the "abortIndexBuild" oplog entry stop the in-progress index build and discard the build job. See [Index Build Process](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#std-label-index-build-process) for detailed documentation on the index build process. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropIndex.md#stop-in-progress-index-builds · keywords: dropIndex, index, index build, db.collection.dropIndex() · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/dropIndexes.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropIndexes.md
- [passage] The index only supports queries on fields included in the `wildcardProjection` object. In this example, MongoDB performs a collection scan for the following query because it includes a field that is not present in the `wildcardProjection` object: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/create-wildcard-index-multiple-fields.md#results · keywords: index, wildcard index, wildcardProjection
- [passage] The index **does not** support queries on `attributes.memory`, because that field was omitted from the index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/create-wildcard-index-multiple-fields.md#results · keywords: index, wildcard index, attributes.memory
- [passage] 4. Secondary members continue to process any new write operations into the index while waiting for the primary to confirm a quorum of votes. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#index-builds-in-replicated-environments · keywords: index, index build
- [passage] Click the closed-eye icon on the right that appears when you hover over your selected index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/indexes.md#hide-or-unhide-an-index · keywords: hidden index, index · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/compass/indexes.md
- [passage] Because indexes are fully maintained while hidden, the index is immediately available for use once unhidden. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden.md#unhide-an-existing-index · keywords: hidden index, index
- [statement] A community forum test reported that hiding an index on the primary also showed as hidden on a secondary, i.e. the hide replicates (anecdotal, single test). Because the toggle is a collMod oplog entry, it is expected to replicate. — https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/hiding-index-replication-ops-manager/270730 · keywords: hidden index, index, Hidden Indexes
- [passage] Wildcard indexes are sparse indexes. They do not support queries when an indexed field does not exist. A wildcard index will index the document if the wildcard field has a null value. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes/ · keywords: index, wildcard index · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/reference/restrictions.md
- [passage] Wildcard indexes do not support mixing inclusion and exclusion statements in the wildcardProjection document except when explicitly including the _id field. For more information on wildcardProjection, see the parameter documentation. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes/ · keywords: index, wildcard index · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndexes.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndex.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/create-wildcard-index-multiple-fields.md
- [passage] The index records for `ship.coordinates` and `ship.captains` do not include the array position for each element. Wildcard indexes ignore array element positions when recording the element into the index. However, wildcard indexes can still support queries that include explicit array indices. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/reference/embedded-object-behavior.md#queries-with-explicit-array-indices · keywords: index, wildcard index, ship.coordinates, ship.captains
- [passage] Unfortunately, it is expensive to create a lot of individual indexes to cover all of the possible queries. A wildcard index is a good alternative to creating a large number of individual indexes because one wildcard index can efficiently cover many potential queries. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/index-wildcard-compound.md#search-using-the-attribute-pattern · keywords: index, wildcard index
- [passage] When using `wildcardProjection` with compound wildcard indexes, the following rules apply: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/reference/restrictions.md#wildcardprojection-validation-rules · keywords: index, wildcard index, wildcardProjection
- [fact] Wildcard indexes are intended for queries on fields whose names are unknown, vary between documents, or live in inconsistent embedded documents. MongoDB's manual says to use them only when the indexed fields are unknown or may change, and that they do not perform as well as targeted indexes on specific fields. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-wildcard/ · keywords: index, wildcard index, Wildcard and Compound Wildcard Indexes
- [passage] When a secondary node receives a commitIndexBuild oplog entry, the node stops further oplog applications until the local index build can be committed. Index builds can take anywhere from moments to days to complete, so the replication lag can be significant if the secondary node builds more slowly than the primary. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setindexcommitquorum/ · keywords: index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setIndexCommitQuorum.md
- [passage] The commit quorum does not guarantee that indexes on secondaries are ready for use when the command completes. To ensure that a specific number of secondaries are ready for use, set an appropriate write concern. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setindexcommitquorum/ · keywords: commit quorum, index
- [passage] MongoDB begins removing expired documents or time series buckets as soon as the index finishes building on the [primary](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-primary). For more information on the index build process, see [Index Builds on Populated Collections.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#std-label-index-operations) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-ttl.md#timing-of-the-delete-operation · keywords: index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-ttl/
- [passage] - To learn how MongoDB builds indexes, see [Index Build Process.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#std-label-index-build-process) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/create-index.md#learn-more · keywords: index, index build
- [passage] For featureCompatibilityVersion "4.2", createIndexes uses an optimized build process that obtains and holds an exclusive lock on the specified collection at the start and end of the index build. All subsequent operations on the collection must wait until createIndexes releases the exclusive lock. createIndexes allows interleaving read and write operations during the majority of the index build. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes/ · keywords: index, index build
- [passage] For featureCompatibilityVersion "4.0", createIndexes uses the pre-4.2 index build process which by default obtains an exclusive lock on the parent database for the entire duration of the build process. The pre-4.2 build process blocks all operations on the database and all its collections until the operation completed. background indexes do not take an exclusive lock. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes/ · keywords: index, index build
- [passage] When using the default maxNumActiveUserIndexBuilds of 3, the total memory usage for all concurrent index builds can reach up to three times the value of maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes/ · keywords: index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/
- [passage] The primary marks index build as ready only after a simple majority of data-bearing voting members "vote" to commit the index build. For more information on index builds and the voting process, see Index Builds in Replicated Environments. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes/ · keywords: index, index build
- [passage] Applications may encounter reduced performance during index builds, including limited read/write access to the collection. For more information on the index build process, see [Index Builds on Populated Collections](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#std-label-index-operations), including the [Index Builds in Replicated Environments](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#std-label-index-operations-replicated-build) section. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/indexes.md#index-build-performance · keywords: index, index build
- [passage] Building an index in a rolling fashion reduces the resiliency of your cluster and increases index build times. We only recommend using rolling index builds when regular index builds do not meet your needs. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor.md#procedure · keywords: index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/
- [passage] If you decide to continue with a rolling index, consider that they must meet certain conditions to succeed. To ensure your index build succeeds, avoid the following design patterns that commonly trigger a restart loop: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor.md#procedure · keywords: index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/
- [passage] Atlas automatically cancels rolling index builds that don't succeed on all nodes. When a rolling index build completes on some nodes, but fails on others, Atlas cancels the build and removes the index from any nodes that it was successfully built on. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor.md#procedure · keywords: index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/
- [passage] When an index build completes, Atlas generates an [activity feed event](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/activity-feed.md#std-label-view-activity-feed) and sends a notification email to the project owner with the following information: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor.md#procedure · keywords: index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/
- [passage] If you increase `indexBuildMinAvailableDiskSpaceMB`, ensure your server has enough available disk space. Also, if you set `indexBuildMinAvailableDiskSpaceMB` too high, you might needlessly prevent index builds when there is enough available disk space and `indexBuildMinAvailableDiskSpaceMB` could be set lower. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#general-parameters · keywords: index, index build, indexBuildMinAvailableDiskSpaceMB
- [passage] The following sections explain the index properties that you can specify when building an index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-properties.md · keywords: index, index build
- [passage] The preceding command ensures the correct set of shards is targeted for rolling index builds because no migration for the collection will be allowed to commit. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/build-indexes-on-sharded-clusters.md#a-stop-migrations · keywords: index, index build
- [passage] When the index build completes, shutdown the [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) instance. Undo the configuration changes made when starting as a standalone to return to its original configuration and restart. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/build-indexes-on-sharded-clusters.md#c3-restart-the-program-mongod-as-a-replica-set-member · keywords: index, index build, mongod
- [passage] For [featureCompatibilityVersion](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setfeaturecompatibilityversion.md#std-label-view-fcv) `"4.2"`, [`createIndexes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createindexes.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.createIndexes) uses an optimized build process that obtains and holds an exclusive lock on the specified collection at the start and end of the index build. All subsequent operations on the collection must wait until [`createIndexes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createindexes.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.createIndexes) releases the exclusive lock. [`createIndexes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createindexes.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.createIndexes) allows interleaving read and write operations during the majority of the index build. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes.md#concurrency · keywords: index, index build, "4.2", createIndexes
- [passage] For [featureCompatibilityVersion](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setfeaturecompatibilityversion.md#std-label-view-fcv) `"4.0"`, [`createIndexes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createindexes.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.createIndexes) uses the pre-4.2 index build process which by default obtains an exclusive lock on the parent database for the entire duration of the build process. The pre-4.2 build process blocks all operations on the database *and* all its collections until the operation completed. `background` indexes do not take an exclusive lock. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes.md#concurrency · keywords: index, index build, "4.0", createIndexes, background
- [passage] When using the default [`maxNumActiveUserIndexBuilds`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.maxNumActiveUserIndexBuilds) of `3`, the total memory usage for all concurrent index builds can reach up to three times the value of `maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes.md#memory-usage-limit · keywords: index, index build, maxNumActiveUserIndexBuilds, maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md
- [passage] Index builds use an optimized build process that holds an exclusive lock on the collection briefly at the beginning and end of the index build. The rest of the build process yields to interleaving read and write operations. For a detailed description of index build process and locking behavior, see Index Build Process. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md
- [passage] Index builds now obtain an exclusive lock on the collection being indexed only at the start and end of the build. The rest of the build process uses the yielding behavior of background index builds to maximize read-write access to the collection during the build. Index builds still produce efficient index data structures despite the more permissive locking behavior. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md
- [passage] The optimized index build performance is at least on par with background index builds. For workloads with few or no updates received during the build process, optimized index builds can be as fast as a foreground index build on that same data. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md
- [passage] Building indexes when the target collection is under heavy write load can result in reduced write performance and longer index builds. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md
- [passage] For a more detailed description of the index build process, see Index Build Process. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: index, index build
- [passage] The mongod can perform the startup process while recovering index builds. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 5.0, if a node is rolled back to a prior state during the index build, the index build progress is saved to disk. If there is still work to be done when the rollback concludes, the mongod automatically recovers the index build and continues from the saved checkpoint. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md
- [passage] The msg field includes a percentage-complete measurement of the current stage in the index build process. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: index, index build
- [passage] If the mongod replicates a "commitIndexBuild" oplog entry, it finishes draining the side writes table and moves to the next stage in the index build process. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: index, index build
- [passage] The S and X locks at the end of the index build are held only while the mongod drains the remaining side writes and finalizes the index, so they are typically brief. The duration depends on the number of writes remaining in the side writes table when each stage begins. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md
- [passage] Total number of index builds that failed because of data corruption. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md#indexbuilds · keywords: index, index build

- [passage] The [`msg`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentop.md#mongodb-data--currentOp.msg) field includes a percentage-complete measurement of the current stage in the index build process. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#monitor-in-progress-index-builds · keywords: index, index build, msg
- [passage] When the index build completes, shutdown the [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) instance. To return the node to its original configuration, undo the configuration changes that you made when you started the node as a standalone. Then, restart the node as a member of the replica set. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/build-indexes-on-replica-sets.md#4-restart-the-program-mongod-as-a-replica-set-member · keywords: index, index build, mongod
- [passage] The commit quorum does not guarantee that indexes on secondaries are ready for use when the command completes. - [fact] Because a hidden index is fully maintained, unhiding takes effect immediately with no rebuild. Dropping an index, by contrast, requires a full rebuild to undo. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden/ · keywords: hidden index, index, Hidden Indexes
- [fact] Since MongoDB 4.2 all index builds use one optimized process: an exclusive X lock on the collection only at the start and end, with the middle phase downgraded to IX and yielding to reads and writes. The old foreground/background distinction is gone and the `background` option is ignored. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md · keywords: index, index build, Index Build Strategies, background
- [passage] - When a user is creating an index across the shards in a [rolling manner (i.e. manually building the index one by one across the shards)](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/build-indexes-on-sharded-clusters.md) but either fails to build the index for an associated shard or incorrectly builds an index with different specification. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-indexes.md#find-inconsistent-indexes-across-shards · keywords: mongodb-special-indexes-and-index-builds · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md
- [passage] - Changing the `expireAfterSeconds` parameter **does not** trigger a complete index rebuild. However, reducing the `expireAfterSeconds` value can make many documents eligible for immediate deletion, potentially causing performance issues due to the increased delete operations. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-ttl.md#change-the-expireafterseconds-value-for-a-ttl-index · keywords: TTL index, index, expireAfterSeconds
- [passage] For example, consider a sharded collection with shard key `{x: 1}` that spans two shards A and B. Because the `_id` key is not the shard key, the collection could have a document with `_id` value `1` in shard A and another document with `_id` value `1` in shard B. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique.md#sharded-clusters-and-unique-indexes · keywords: index, unique index, {x: 1}, _id,  in shard A and another document with ,  value 
- [passage] When creating an index across the shards in a rolling manner (that is, manually building the index one by one across the shards) but either fails to build the index for an associated shard or incorrectly builds an index with different specification. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: mongodb-special-indexes-and-index-builds
- [passage] Each index suggestion includes an Average Query Targeting score indicating how many documents were read for every document returned for the index's corresponding query shapes. A score of 1 represents very efficient query shapes because every document read matched the query and was returned with the query results. All suggested indexes represent an opportunity to improve query performance. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor.md#query-targeting · keywords: index, index overhead · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/
- [passage] In clustered collections with only a default index on the `_ìd` field (no secondary indexes), the index size appears as zero because the collection does not require a separate index file. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/clustered-collections.md#index-size · keywords: index, index overhead, _ìd
- [passage] You can only use a `wildcardProjection` when the wildcard term is `$**`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/index-wildcard-compound.md#filter-fields-with-a-wildcardprojection · keywords: wildcard index, wildcardProjection, $**

## How-to and procedures

- [passage] To set the [commit quorum](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createindexes.md#std-label-createIndexes-cmd-commitQuorum), use [`createIndexes()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createindexes.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.createIndexes) to specify the `commitQuorum` value. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndexes.md#commit-quorum · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build, createIndexes(), commitQuorum · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndex.md
- [passage] To drop an index, insert the index name and run [db.collection.dropIndex().](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropindex.md#std-label-collection-drop-index) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/index-wildcard-compound.md#use-a-helper-method-to-create-a-wildcard-index · keywords: dropIndex, index, wildcard index
- [passage] To manage the replication lag, the commit quorum delays committing the index build on the primary node until a minimum number of secondaries are also ready to commit the index build. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setindexcommitquorum/ · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setIndexCommitQuorum.md
- [passage] To start an index build with a non-default commit quorum, specify the commitQuorum. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes/ · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build
- [passage] Use the setIndexCommitQuorum command to modify the commit quorum of an in-progress index build. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes/ · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/
- [passage] To start an index build with a non-default commit quorum, specify the [commitQuorum.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createindexes.md#std-label-createIndexes-cmd-commitQuorum) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes.md#replica-sets-and-sharded-clusters · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build
- [passage] To modify the commit quorum required for an in-progress simultaneous index build, use the [`setIndexCommitQuorum`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setindexcommitquorum.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setIndexCommitQuorum) command. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#index-builds-in-replicated-environments · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build, setIndexCommitQuorum
- [passage] To hide a text index, you must specify the index by `name` and not by `keyPattern`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/collMod.md#hide-an-index-from-the-query-planner · keywords: hidden index, index, text index, name, keyPattern
- [passage] To create a wildcard text index, set the index key to the wildcard specifier (`$**`) and set the index value to `text`: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text/create-wildcard-text-index.md · keywords: index, text index, wildcard index, $**, text
- [passage] Create a wildcard text index on the `blog` collection: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text/create-wildcard-text-index.md#procedure · keywords: index, text index, wildcard index, blog
- [passage] Use the dropIndexes command or its shell helpers dropIndex() or dropIndexes() to terminate an in-progress index build. See Stop In-Progress Index Builds for more information. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: dropIndex, index, index build
- [passage] To drop or hide an index by using the Atlas UI, click the Indexes tab, then click the Drop Index or Hide Index icon next to the index. Atlas displays a dialog box to confirm your selection. For more information, see [Manage Atlas Indexes.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/indexes.md#std-label-atlas-ui-indexes) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/drop-indexes.md#drop-or-hide-an-index · keywords: dropIndex, hidden index, index
- [passage] To create a `hidden` index, use the [`db.collection.createIndex()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createindex.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.createIndex) method with the [hidden](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createindex.md#std-label-method-createIndex-hidden) option set to `true`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden.md#create-a-hidden-index · keywords: hidden index, index, hidden, db.collection.createIndex(), true · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.unhideIndex.md
- [passage] To use the `hidden` option with [`db.collection.createIndex()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createindex.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.createIndex), you must have [featureCompatibilityVersion](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setfeaturecompatibilityversion.md#std-label-view-fcv) set to `7.0` or greater. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden.md#create-a-hidden-index · keywords: hidden index, index, hidden, db.collection.createIndex(), 7.0
- [passage] To verify, run [`db.collection.getIndexes()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.getindexes.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.getIndexes) on the `restaurants` collection: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden.md#unhide-an-existing-index · keywords: hidden index, index, db.collection.getIndexes(), restaurants

- [passage] To create a [partial](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md#std-label-index-type-partial) compound wildcard index, you can use the `partialFilterExpression` option to specify a filter expression so that the index only includes documents that match the filter condition. `partialFilterExpression` can cover fields included or not included in the index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/index-wildcard-compound.md#create-a-partial-compound-wildcard-index · keywords: index, wildcard index, partialFilterExpression
- [passage] To include or exclude fields in a wildcard index, specify the chosen fields in the `wildcardProjection` option: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/create-wildcard-index-multiple-fields.md · keywords: index, wildcard index, wildcardProjection
- [passage] To learn how to use wildcard projection with a compound wildcard index to filter fields, see [Filter Fields with a `wildcardProjection`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/index-wildcard-compound.md#std-label-wc-compound-index-wcProject) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/create-wildcard-index-multiple-fields.md#learn-more · keywords: index, wildcard index, wildcardProjection
- [passage] To learn how to specify a wildcard index, see [Create a Wildcard Index.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/indexes.md#std-label-atlas-ui-wildcard-index) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/indexes.md#create-an-index · keywords: index, wildcard index · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/compass/indexes.md
- [passage] To create a wildcard index on a single field, use the [`db.collection.createIndex()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createindex.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.createIndex) method and include the wildcard specifier (`$**`) in the index key: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/create-wildcard-index-single-field.md · keywords: index, wildcard index, db.collection.createIndex(), $**
- [passage] To create a wildcard index on all fields (excluding `_id`), use the wildcard specifier (`$**`) as the index key: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/create-wildcard-index-all-fields.md · keywords: index, wildcard index, _id, $**
- [passage] Use [`mongosh`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongosh) to monitor index creation. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/create-index.md#results · keywords: index, index build, mongosh
- [passage] To unhide the index, you can specify either the index key specification document or the index name to the [`db.collection.unhideIndex()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.unhideindex.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.unhideIndex) method. The following specifies the index name: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.unhideIndex.md#example · keywords: hidden index, index, db.collection.unhideIndex() · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.hideIndex.md
- [passage] To hide or unhide existing indexes, you can use the following [`mongosh`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongosh) methods: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndexes.md#hidden-option · keywords: hidden index, index, mongosh · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndex.md
- [passage] Avoid performing rolling index and replicated index build processes concurrently as it might lead to unexpected issues, such as broken builds and crash loops. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/build-indexes-on-sharded-clusters.md#about-this-task · keywords: index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-indexes.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/build-indexes-on-replica-sets.md
- [passage] Use db.currentOp() to monitor the progress of ongoing index builds. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: index, index build
