- [passage] Similarly, wildcard indexes cannot support exact **inequality** matches on documents and arrays. For example, a wildcard index on `product_attributes` cannot support the following queries: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/reference/restrictions.md#equality-matches-on-documents-and-arrays · keywords: index, wildcard index, product_attributes
- [passage] Wildcard indexes are [sparse](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md#std-label-index-type-sparse) and do not index empty fields. Therefore, wildcard indexes cannot support queries for documents where a field does not exist. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/reference/restrictions.md#field-does-not-exist · keywords: index, wildcard index
- [passage] For example, consider an `inventory` collection with a wildcard index on `product_attributes`. The wildcard index cannot support all of the predicates in the following query: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/reference/restrictions.md#multi-field-query-predicates · keywords: index, wildcard index, inventory, product_attributes
- [passage] If the above conditions are not met, MongoDB cannot use the wildcard index for the sort. MongoDB does not support [`sort()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md#mongodb-method-cursor.sort) operations that require a different index from that of the query predicate. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/reference/restrictions.md#queries-with-sort · keywords: index, wildcard index, sort()
- [fact] wildcardProjection works only when the wildcard term is $** (not a path like someFields.$**). Wildcard indexes omit _id by default; include it with $** or by adding _id: 1 to wildcardProjection. A field cannot appear both in the wildcard pattern and as a regular compound term; use exclusions in wildcardProjection to remove it. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/upcoming/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/reference/restrictions/ · keywords: index, wildcard index, Wildcard and Compound Wildcard Indexes
- [statement] Starting in MongoDB 8.3, 8.2.4, 8.0.18 and 7.0.29, stricter wildcardProjection validation applies to compound wildcard indexes: projection cannot be empty; inclusions and exclusions cannot be mixed except for _id; included fields cannot overlap regular index fields; an _id-only exclusion needs _id as a regular index field; an exclusion projection must exclude all regular index fields. Existing non-compliant indexes keep working; new ones cannot be created. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/upcoming/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/reference/restrictions/ · keywords: index, wildcard index, Wildcard and Compound Wildcard Indexes
- [statement] Wildcard indexes store the contents of documents and arrays, not the containers, so exact equality or inequality on a whole embedded document or array (e.g. { "product_attributes": { price: 29.99 } }) is unsupported (matching {} is the exception). If a field is an array in any document, the index cannot support $ne null on it. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/upcoming/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/reference/restrictions/ · keywords: index, wildcard index, Wildcard and Compound Wildcard Indexes
- [fact] Consolidating many single-field indexes into one wildcard index helps stay under the 64-index-per-collection limit. A collection may hold several wildcard indexes and they may overlap other indexes. Compound wildcard indexes are sparse: a document is indexed if it has at least one of the compound fields. — https://mongodb.com/docs/v7.0/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/index-wildcard-compound · keywords: index, wildcard index, Wildcard and Compound Wildcard Indexes
- [passage] For replica sets and sharded clusters, using a [rolling procedure](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/build-indexes-on-replica-sets.md#std-label-index-build-on-replica-sets) to create a unique index requires that you stop all writes to the collection during the procedure. If you cannot stop all writes to the collection during the procedure, do not use the rolling procedure. Instead, to build your unique index on the collection you must either: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique.md#building-unique-index-on-replica-sets-and-sharded-clusters · keywords: mongodb-special-indexes-and-index-builds
- [passage] In self-hosted MongoDB deployments, you can change the memory limit for index builds by setting the maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes parameter. Increasing this parameter is only necessary in rare cases. Such cases include running many simultaneous index builds with a single createIndexes command or indexing a data set larger than 500GB. You can also set maxNumActiveUserIndexBuilds to adjust how many index builds can run concurrently. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes/ · keywords: index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md
- [passage] For workloads which cannot tolerate performance decrease due to index builds, consider building indexes in a rolling fashion. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor.md#procedure · keywords: index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/
- [passage] A new index build cannot be started and a current index build is cancelled if the available disk space is below `indexBuildMinAvailableDiskSpaceMB`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#general-parameters · keywords: index, index build, indexBuildMinAvailableDiskSpaceMB
- [passage] Limits the amount of memory that simultaneous [index builds](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#std-label-index-build-process) on one collection may consume for their duration. The specified amount of memory is shared between all indexes built using a single [`createIndexes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createindexes.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.createIndexes) command or its shell helper [`db.collection.createIndexes()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createindexes.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.createIndexes). Increasing the limit may avoid negative performance impacts in some cases, such as when building numerous indexes simultaneously with a single [`createIndexes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createindexes.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.createIndexes) command and/or when working with index key data set sizes that exceed 500GB. The memory consumed by an index build is separate from the WiredTiger cache memory (see [`cacheSizeGB`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options.md#mongodb-setting-storage.wiredTiger.engineConfig.cacheSizeGB)). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#general-parameters · keywords: index, index build, createIndexes, db.collection.createIndexes(), cacheSizeGB
- [passage] Sets the maximum number of index build requests that MongoDB can perform concurrently. `maxNumActiveUserIndexBuilds` is a global limit that applies for all collections. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#general-parameters · keywords: index, index build, maxNumActiveUserIndexBuilds
- [passage] System indexes are not limited to `maxNumActiveUserIndexBuilds`, however a system index build counts against the limit for user index builds. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#general-parameters · keywords: index, index build, maxNumActiveUserIndexBuilds
- [passage] After the server reaches `maxNumActiveUserIndexBuilds`, it blocks additional user index builds until the number of concurrent index builds drops below the `maxNumActiveUserIndexBuilds` limit. If an index build is blocked, the server logs this message: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#general-parameters · keywords: index, index build, maxNumActiveUserIndexBuilds · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md
- [passage] The following command sets a limit of 4 concurrent index builds: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#general-parameters · keywords: index, index build
- [passage] [Hidden indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden.md#std-label-index-type-hidden) are not visible to the [query planner](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-query-plans-query-optimization) and cannot be used to support a query. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-properties.md#hidden-indexes · keywords: hidden index, index · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden.md
- [passage] - If you use [`hint()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) on a [hidden index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden.md) or an index that doesn't exist, the operation returns an error. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#behavior · keywords: hidden index, index, hint()
- [passage] Rolling indexes build indexes on the applicable nodes sequentially and may reduce the performance impact of an index build if your deployment's average CPU utilization exceeds (N-1)/N-10% where N is the number of CPU threads available to mongod of if the WiredTiger cache fill ratio regularly exceeds 90%. If your deployment does not meet this criteria, use the default index build. You can't create a rolling index on an M0 free cluster or M2/M5 shared cluster. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-api-rollingIndex.md · keywords: index, index build
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 7.1, index builds are improved with faster error reporting and increased failure resilience. You can also set the minimum available disk space required for index builds using the new [`indexBuildMinAvailableDiskSpaceMB`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.indexBuildMinAvailableDiskSpaceMB) parameter, which stops index builds if disk space is too low. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndexes.md#index-builds · keywords: index, index build, indexBuildMinAvailableDiskSpaceMB · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndex.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md
- [passage] - You cannot hide a clustered index. See [Hidden indexes.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden.md) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/clustered-collections.md#limitations · keywords: hidden index, index
- [passage] Increased resilience for your deployment. If an index build error occurs, a secondary member can request that the primary member stop an index build and the secondary member does not crash. A request to stop an index build is not always possible: if a member has already voted to commit the index, then the secondary cannot request that the index build stop and the secondary crashes (similar to MongoDB 7.0 and earlier). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: index, index build
- [passage] An index build error can cause a secondary member to crash. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: index, index build
- [passage] If the number of concurrent index builds reaches the limit specified by maxNumActiveUserIndexBuilds, the server blocks additional index builds until the number of concurrent index builds drops below the limit. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: index, index build
- [passage] If no keys in the constraint violation table produce a key generation error or if the table is empty, the mongod drops the table and creates a "commitIndexBuild" oplog entry. Secondaries can complete the associated index build after replicating the oplog entry. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: index, index build
- [passage] If any key in the constraint violation table still produces a key generation error, the mongod aborts the build and throws an error. The mongod creates an associated "abortIndexBuild" oplog entry to indicate that secondaries should abort and discard the index build job. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: index, index build
- [passage] The [`maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes) limit applies to all index builds initiated by user commands like [`createIndexes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createindexes.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.createIndexes) or administrative processes like [initial sync.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-sync.md#std-label-replica-set-sync) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits.md#indexes · keywords: index, index build, maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes, createIndexes
- [passage] An [initial sync](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-sync.md#std-label-replica-set-sync) populates only one collection at a time and has no risk of exceeding the memory limit. However, it is possible for a user to start index builds on multiple collections in multiple databases simultaneously. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits.md#indexes · keywords: index, index build
- [passage] Hidden indexes are not visible to the query planner and cannot be used to support a query. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden/ · keywords: hidden index, index
- [passage] You cannot cursor.hint() a hidden index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden/ · keywords: hidden index, index
- [fact] Restrictions: the _id index cannot be hidden, and cursor.hint() cannot force a hidden index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden/ · keywords: hidden index, index, Hidden Indexes
- [fact] Self-hosted index builds default to maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes=200 per createIndexes command, split equally across the indexes in that command, spilling to _tmp under --dbpath. With the default maxNumActiveUserIndexBuilds=3, total can reach 3x. Raising it is rarely needed (many indexes in one command, or data over 500GB). On Atlas the defaults vary by tier and maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes cannot be changed. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md · keywords: index, index build, Index Build Strategies
- [passage] - Other [`findAndModify`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/findandmodify.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.findAndModify) operations either update the newly-inserted document or fail due to a unique key collision. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/findAndModify.md#upsert-with-unique-index · keywords: index, unique index, findAndModify
- [passage] - Other [`findOneAndUpdate()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.findoneandupdate.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.findOneAndUpdate) operations either update the newly-inserted document or fail due to a unique key collision. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.findAndModify.md#upsert-with-unique-index · keywords: index, unique index, findOneAndUpdate()
- [passage] Queryable Encryption compatible drivers configured for automatic encryption [support some operations for automatic encryption](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/reference/supported-operations.md#std-label-qe-reference-automatic-encryption-supported-operations). For unsupported read and write operations, the underlying library can't introspect the index catalog to identify a given field as unique. Applications can't rely on automatic encryption validation to prevent unique constraint violations on randomly-encrypted fields. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/reference/limitations.md#unique-indexes · keywords: index, unique index
- [passage] - **Remove the failed index**: Atlas removes the index entirely, and you must rebuild it. This happens when the index cannot be recovered. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/atlas-search-alerts.md#alert-conditions · keywords: mongodb-special-indexes-and-index-builds
- [passage] To update the commitQuorum, member replica set nodes must have members[n].buildIndexes set to true. If any voting nodes have members[n].buildIndexes set to false, you can't use the default "votingMembers" commit quorum. Either configure all nodes with members[n].buildIndexes set to true, or select a different commit quorum. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setindexcommitquorum/ · keywords: commit quorum · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes/
- [passage] Replica set nodes with buildIndexes set to false can't be included in a commit quorum. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setindexcommitquorum/ · keywords: commit quorum
- [passage] Replica set nodes with [buildIndexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/replica-configuration.md#std-label-replica-set-configuration-buildIndexes) set to `false` can't be included in a commit quorum. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setIndexCommitQuorum.md#behavior · keywords: commit quorum, false

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [passage] | Parameter | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `unique` | boolean | Optional. Specifies that each index specified in the `keyPatterns` array is a [unique index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique.md#std-label-index-type-unique). Unique indexes will not accept insertion or update of documents where the index key value matches an existing value in the index. Specify `true` to create a unique index. The default value is `false`. The option is *unavailable* for [hashed indexes.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-hashed.md#std-label-index-hashed-index) | | `name` | string | Optional. The name of the index. If unspecified, MongoDB generates an index name by concatenating the names of the indexed fields and the sort order. Options specified to [`db.collection.createIndexes()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createindexes.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.createIndexes) apply to **all** of the index specifications included in the key pattern array. Since index names must be unique, you may only specify name if you are creating a single index using [`db.collection.createIndexes()`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createindexes.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.createIndexes) | | `partialFilterExpression` | document | Optional. If specified, the indexes only reference documents that match the filter expression. See [Partial Indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md#std-label-index-type-partial) for more information. A filter expression can include: equality expressions (i.e. `field: value` or using the [`$eq`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/eq.md#mongodb-query-op.-eq) operator); [`$exists: true`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/exists.md#mongodb-query-op.-exists) expression; [`$gt`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/gt.md#mongodb-query-op.-gt), [`$gte`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/gte.md#mongodb-query-op.-gte), [`$lt`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/lt.md#mongodb-query-op.-lt), [`$lte`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/lte.md#mongodb-query-op.-lte) expressions; [`$type`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/type.md#mongodb-query-op.-type) expressions; [`$and`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/and.md#mongodb-query-op.-and) operator; [`$or`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/or.md#mongodb-query-op.-or) operator; [`$in`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/in.md#mongodb-query-op.-in) operator; [`$geoWithin`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/geowithin.md#mongodb-query-op.-geoWithin) operator; [`$geoIntersects`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/geointersects.md#mongodb-query-op.-geoIntersects) operator You can specify a `partialFilterExpression` option for all MongoDB [index types.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types.md#std-label-index-types) | | `sparse` | boolean | Optional. If `true`, the indexes only reference documents with the specified fields. These indexes use less space but behave differently in some situations (particularly sorts). The default value is `false`. See [Sparse Indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md#std-label-index-type-sparse) for more information. The following index types are sparse by default and ignore this option: [2dsphere](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2dsphere.md#std-label-2dsphere-index); [2d](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2d.md#std-label-2d-index); [Text](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text.md#std-label-index-type-text) For a compound index that includes `2dsphere` index keys and keys for other types, only the `2dsphere` index fields determine whether the index references a document. [Partial indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md#std-label-index-type-partial) have a superset of the sparse index functionality. Unless your application has a specific requirement, use partial indexes instead of sparse indexes. | | `expireAfterSeconds` | integer | Optional. Specifies a value, in seconds, as a time to live ([TTL](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-TTL)) to control how long MongoDB retains documents in this collection. This option only applies to [TTL](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-TTL) indexes. See [Expire Data from Collections by Setting TTL](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/expire-data.md#std-label-ttl-collections) for more information. If you use TTL indexes created before MongoDB 5.0, or if you want to sync data created in MongDB 5.0 with a pre-5.0 installation, see [Indexes Configured Using NaN](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/expire-data.md#std-label-expireData-warning) to avoid misconfiguration issues. The TTL index `expireAfterSeconds` value must be within `0` and `2147483647` inclusive. | | [hidden](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createindexes.md#std-label-method-createIndexes-hidden) | boolean | Optional. A flag that determines whether the index is [hidden](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden.md#std-label-index-type-hidden) from the query planner. A hidden index is not evaluated as part of the query plan selection. Default is `false`. | | `storageEngine` | document | Optional. Allows users to configure the storage engine for the created indexes. The `storageEngine` option should take the following form: `storageEngine: { <storage-engine-name>: <options> }` Storage engine configuration options specified when creating indexes are validated and logged to the [oplog](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-oplog) during replication to support replica sets with members that use different storage engines. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndexes.md#options-for-all-index-types · keywords: TTL index, hashed index, hidden index, index, index overhead, unique index
- [passage] | Parameter | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `unique` | boolean | Optional. Creates a unique index so that the collection will not accept insertion or update of documents where the index key value matches an existing value in the index. Specify `true` to create a unique index. The default value is `false`. The option is *unavailable* for [hashed indexes.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-hashed.md#std-label-index-hashed-index) | | `name` | string | Optional. The name of the index. If unspecified, MongoDB generates an index name by concatenating the names of the indexed fields and the sort order. | | `partialFilterExpression` | document | Optional. If specified, the index only references documents that match the filter expression. See [Partial Indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md) for more information. A filter expression can include: equality expressions (i.e. `field: value` or using the [`$eq`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/eq.md#mongodb-query-op.-eq) operator); [`$exists: true`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/exists.md#mongodb-query-op.-exists) expression; [`$gt`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/gt.md#mongodb-query-op.-gt), [`$gte`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/gte.md#mongodb-query-op.-gte), [`$lt`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/lt.md#mongodb-query-op.-lt), [`$lte`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/lte.md#mongodb-query-op.-lte) expressions; [`$type`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/type.md#mongodb-query-op.-type) expressions; [`$and`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/and.md#mongodb-query-op.-and) operator; [`$or`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/or.md#mongodb-query-op.-or) operator; [`$in`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/in.md#mongodb-query-op.-in) operator; [`$geoWithin`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/geowithin.md#mongodb-query-op.-geoWithin) operator; [`$geoIntersects`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/geointersects.md#mongodb-query-op.-geoIntersects) operator You can specify a `partialFilterExpression` option for all MongoDB [index types.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types.md#std-label-index-types) | | `sparse` | boolean | Optional. If `true`, the index only references documents with the specified field. These indexes use less space but behave differently in some situations (particularly sorts). The default value is `false`. See [Sparse Indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md) for more information. The following index types are sparse by default and ignore this option: [2dsphere](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2dsphere.md#std-label-2dsphere-index); [2d](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2d.md#std-label-2d-index); [Text](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text.md#std-label-index-type-text) For a compound index that includes `2dsphere` index keys and keys for other types, only the `2dsphere` index fields determine whether the index references a document. [Partial indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md#std-label-index-type-partial) have a superset of the sparse index functionality. Unless your application has a specific requirement, use partial indexes instead of sparse indexes. | | `expireAfterSeconds` | integer | Optional. Specifies a value, in seconds, as a time to live ([TTL](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-TTL)) to control how long MongoDB retains documents in this collection. This option only applies to [TTL](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-TTL) indexes. See [Expire Data from Collections by Setting TTL](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/expire-data.md#std-label-ttl-collections) for more information. If you use TTL indexes created before MongoDB 5.0, or if you want to sync data created in MongDB 5.0 with a pre-5.0 installation, see [Indexes Configured Using NaN](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/expire-data.md#std-label-expireData-warning) to avoid misconfiguration issues. The TTL index `expireAfterSeconds` value must be within `0` and `2147483647` inclusive. | | [hidden](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createindex.md#std-label-method-createIndex-hidden) | boolean | Optional. A flag that determines whether the index is [hidden](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden.md#std-label-index-type-hidden) from the query planner. A hidden index is not evaluated as part of the query plan selection. Default is `false`. | | `storageEngine` | document | Optional. Allows users to configure the storage engine on a per-index basis when creating an index. The `storageEngine` option should take the following form: `storageEngine: { <storage-engine-name>: <options> }` Storage engine configuration options specified when creating indexes are validated and logged to the [oplog](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-oplog) during replication to support replica sets with members that use different storage engines. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndex.md#options-for-all-index-types · keywords: TTL index, hashed index, hidden index, index, unique index, unique
- [fact] Index builds take exclusive X locks only at start and end, plus a shared S lock during the final side-writes drain. These blocks cover reads, writes, replicated writes and metadata commands on the collection. Writes during the build are held in a side writes table, and key-constraint violations are recorded and checked at commit time rather than rejecting writes. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build, Index Build Conflicts and Commit Quorum and In-Flight Builds
- [passage] If the mongod crashes instead of shutting down cleanly, the index build cannot resume regardless of the commit quorum setting. The index build restarts from the beginning when the mongod comes back online. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md
- [passage] | Behavior Starting in MongoDB 7.1 | Behavior in Earlier MongoDB Versions | | --- | --- | | Index errors found during the collection scan phase, except duplicate key errors, are returned immediately and then the index build stops. Earlier MongoDB versions return errors in the commit phase, which occurs near the end of the index build. MongoDB 7.1 helps you to rapidly diagnose index errors. For example, if an incompatible index value format is found, the error is returned to you immediately. | Index build errors can take a long time to be returned compared to MongoDB 7.1 because the errors are returned near the end of the index build in the commit phase. | | Increased resilience for your deployment. If an index build error occurs, a [secondary](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-secondary) member can request that the [primary](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-primary) member stop an index build and the secondary member does not crash. A request to stop an index build is not always possible: if a member has already voted to commit the index, then the secondary cannot request that the index build stop and the secondary crashes (similar to MongoDB 7.0 and earlier). | An index build error can cause a secondary member to crash. | | Improved disk space management for index builds. An index build may be automatically stopped if the available disk space is below the minimum specified in the [`indexBuildMinAvailableDiskSpaceMB`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.indexBuildMinAvailableDiskSpaceMB) parameter. If a member has already voted to commit the index, then the index build is not stopped. | An index build is not stopped if there is insufficient available disk space. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndexes.md#index-builds · keywords: index, index build, unique index, indexBuildMinAvailableDiskSpaceMB · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndex.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md
- [passage] If, however, the impact is negative, the user can unhide the index instead of having to recreate a dropped index. And because indexes are fully maintained while hidden, the indexes are immediately available for use once unhidden. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropIndex.md#hidden-indexes · keywords: hidden index, index · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/dropIndexes.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropIndexes.md
- [fact] MongoDB 7.1 added early error reporting during the collection scan (except duplicate keys), a secondary can ask the primary to abort a failing build instead of crashing (unless it already voted to commit), and indexBuildMinAvailableDiskSpaceMB can stop builds when free disk is low; earlier versions do not stop on low disk. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md · keywords: index, index build, Index Build Strategies
- [passage] When a wildcard index encounters an array, it traverses the array to index its elements. If the array element is itself an array (an embedded array), the index records the *entire* embedded array as a value instead of traversing its contents. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/reference/embedded-object-behavior.md#wildcard-indexes-on-arrays · keywords: index, wildcard index
- [fact] Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB diverges: its docs say wildcard indexes there can support multiple fields in query predicates with no performance difference versus per-property indexes, but they cannot be compound, TTL or unique, and cannot use wildcardProjection with multiple specific fields (include or exclude). Cosmos advises individually indexed paths for write-heavy workloads because wildcard indexing of many-field documents raises write RU charges. Do not assume Cosmos behavior matches MongoDB Server. — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/mongodb/indexing · keywords: index, wildcard index, Wildcard and Compound Wildcard Indexes
- [passage] You can use hidden indexes to evaluate the potential impact of dropping an index without actually dropping it. If the impact is negative, you can unhide the index instead of having to recreate a dropped index. Hidden indexes are fully maintained and can be used immediately once unhidden. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-properties.md#hidden-indexes · keywords: hidden index, index
- [passage] Index build errors can take a long time to be returned compared to MongoDB 7.1 because the errors are returned near the end of the index build in the commit phase. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: index, index build
- [passage] This differs from interrupted index builds on Atlas Core clusters and self-managed deployments, which are described in the following sections. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: index, index build
- [passage] An index build can resume from a saved checkpoint only once. If the mongod restarts again while that same index build is still in progress, the build restarts from the beginning instead of resuming from a checkpoint. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md
- [passage] By hiding an index from the planner, you can evaluate the potential impact of dropping an index without actually dropping the index. If the impact is negative, you can unhide the index instead of having to recreate a dropped index. And because indexes are fully maintained while hidden, the indexes are immediately available for use once unhidden. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.hideIndex/ · keywords: hidden index, index · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.hideIndex.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden/
- [fact] A hidden index is not visible to the query planner and cannot support a query. Hiding it lets you evaluate the impact of dropping the index without dropping it; if the impact is negative, you unhide it instead of rebuilding it. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden/ · keywords: hidden index, index, Hidden Indexes
- [passage] Starting in version 6.0, you can add a secondary index to any field in a time series collection. MongoDB indexes time series collections by [buckets](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing.md#std-label-timeseries-bucketing) of documents as opposed to individual documents. Time series buckets contain documents with shared metaField values, ordered by timeField values that are close together. MongoDB indexes the minimum and maximum values of all fields, except the metaField. Indexing buckets instead of individual documents reduces index size and improves query efficiency. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-index.md · keywords: index, index overhead

## Facts and statements

- [fact] Stop an in-flight build with dropIndexes (or dropIndex helpers), not killOp: the docs say not to use killOp on replica sets or sharded clusters. dropIndexes aborts the build via abortIndexBuild, and it must name every index from the same createIndexes batch. Percona's post instead says killOp cancels the build, which conflicts with the docs. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: commit quorum, dropIndex, index, index build, Index Build Conflicts and Commit Quorum and In-Flight Builds
- [statement] Interrupted builds: on a replica set with default commit quorum, a clean shutdown or SIGTERM saves progress and the build resumes once from the checkpoint (since 5.0 also across rollbacks); a crash restarts from scratch. A member restarted as standalone leaves the build paused until dropped. A standalone mongod loses the build entirely. Use dropIndexes, not killOp, to stop a replicated build. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md · keywords: commit quorum, dropIndex, index, index build, Index Build Strategies
- [passage] | Option | Description | More Information | | --- | --- | --- | | Create unique index | Ensure that the indexed fields do not store duplicate values. | [Unique Indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique/) | | Index name | Specify a name for the index. | [Specify an Index Name](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/create-index/specify-index-name.md#std-label-specify-index-name) | | Create a TTL (Time to Live) index | Delete documents automatically after a specified number of seconds since the indexed field value. | [TTL Indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-ttl/) | | Partial filter expression | Index only the documents which match the specified filter expression. For example: The following partial filter expression only indexes documents where the `timezone` field exists: `{ "timezone": { "$exists": true } }` | [Partial Indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial/) | | Wildcard projection | Support unknown or arbitrary fields which match the specified projection in the index. To use a wildcard projection, set your index field name to `$**`. This directs Compass to use all fields in the document (excluding `_id`). For example: Consider the following wildcard projection document: `{ "product_attributes.elements" : 1, "product_attributes.resistance" : 1 }` If your index field name is `$**`, your index only includes the values of the fields in that projection. | [Create a Wildcard Index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/compass/indexes.md#std-label-compass-wildcard-index) | | Use custom collation | Create a custom collation for the index by typing or pasting the collation document in the text box. | [Collation Document](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation/#collation-document) | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/compass/indexes.md#create-an-index · keywords: TTL index, index, unique index, wildcard index, timezone, { "timezone": { "$exists": true } }
- [passage] Each [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) in the replica set or sharded cluster *must* have [featureCompatibilityVersion](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setfeaturecompatibilityversion.md#std-label-set-fcv) set to at least `4.4` to start index builds simultaneously across replica set members. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndexes.md#commit-quorum · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build, mongod, 4.4 · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndex.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setIndexCommitQuorum.md
- [passage] There are important differences between [commit quorums](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createindexes.md#std-label-createIndexes-cmd-commitQuorum) and [write concerns:](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/write-concern.md#std-label-write-concern) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes.md#commit-quorum-contrasted-with-write-concern · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setIndexCommitQuorum.md
- [fact] Replicated build protocol: primary writes a startIndexBuild oplog entry; secondaries build after replicating it and vote by writing to an internal replicated collection on the primary; once the quorum is met and no key-constraint violations remain, the primary writes commitIndexBuild. On a violation the primary aborts and writes abortIndexBuild, and secondaries discard the build job. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build, Index Build Conflicts and Commit Quorum and In-Flight Builds
- [fact] setIndexCommitQuorum changes the quorum of an in-progress build. indexNames must list the entire set of in-progress builds from one createIndexes call, and it has no effect on builds started with commitQuorum 0. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setindexcommitquorum/ · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build, Index Build Conflicts and Commit Quorum and In-Flight Builds
- [statement] Bug SERVER-56976: a build already waiting for votes did not pick up a setIndexCommitQuorum change (found after a half-finished rolling build left one secondary with the index, which treated startIndexBuild as a no-op). Affected 4.4.6 and 5.0.0; fixed in 4.4.7 and 5.0.0-rc0/5.1.0-rc0. On old 4.4.x/5.0.0 binaries lowering the quorum may not unstick a build. — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-56976 · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build, Index Build Conflicts and Commit Quorum and In-Flight Builds
- [fact] Do not run rolling index builds and replicated (simultaneous) builds concurrently; the docs warn of broken builds and crash loops. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build, Index Build Conflicts and Commit Quorum and In-Flight Builds
- [passage] If the options specification had been split into multiple documents like this: `{ unique: true }, { sparse: true, expireAfterSeconds: 3600 }` the index creation operation would have failed. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndex.md#options · keywords: TTL index, index, index build, unique index, { unique: true }, { sparse: true, expireAfterSeconds: 3600 }
- [fact] Apart from planner visibility, a hidden index behaves like an unhidden one: a hidden unique index still enforces its unique constraint, a hidden TTL index still expires documents, and the index still appears in listIndexes and getIndexes() with "hidden": true. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden/ · keywords: TTL index, hidden index, index, unique index, Hidden Indexes
- [passage] Consider [hiding indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/drop-indexes.md#std-label-hidden-indexes) before you drop them. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/drop-indexes.md#drop-or-hide-an-index · keywords: dropIndex, hidden index, index
- [passage] In the Performance Advisor tab, click Explore Recommendations on the Drop Indexes card. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/drop-indexes.md#drop-or-hide-an-index · keywords: dropIndex, hidden index, index
- [passage] 5. On the index that you want to drop or hide, click Drop Index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/drop-indexes.md#drop-or-hide-an-index · keywords: dropIndex, hidden index, index
- [passage] The setIndexCommitQuorum command sets minimum number of data-bearing members that must be prepared to commit their local index builds before the primary node will commit the index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setindexcommitquorum/ · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setIndexCommitQuorum.md
- [passage] The minimum number of data-bearing replica set members (i.e. commit quorum), including the primary, that must report a successful index build before the primary marks the indexes as ready. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setindexcommitquorum/ · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes/

- [passage] Index builds use commit quorums. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setindexcommitquorum/ · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md
- [passage] The commit quorum specifies how many data-bearing voting members, or which voting members, including the primary, must be prepared to commit a simultaneous index build before the primary will execute the commit. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setindexcommitquorum/ · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/
- [passage] Index builds on a replica set or sharded cluster build simultaneously across all data-bearing replica set members. For sharded clusters, the index build occurs only on shards containing data for the collection being indexed. The primary requires a minimum number of data-bearing voting members (i.e commit quorum), including itself, that must complete the build before marking the index as ready for use. See Index Builds in Replicated Environments for more information. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setindexcommitquorum/ · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndexes.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndex.md
- [passage] By default, index builds use "votingMembers" commit quorum, or all data-bearing voting replica set members. The following operation modifies the index build commit quorum to "majority", or a simple majority of data-bearing voting members:. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setindexcommitquorum/ · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setIndexCommitQuorum.md
- [passage] MongoDB marks index builds in various stages, including waiting on commit quorum, as an idle connection by setting the `active` field to `false`. The `idleConnections: true` setting includes these idle connections in the `$currentOp` output. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/create-index.md#results · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build, active, false, idleConnections: true · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/currentOp.md
- [passage] If a data-bearing voting node becomes unreachable and the commitQuorum is set to the default votingMembers, index builds can hang until that node comes back online. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes/ · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/
- [passage] commitQuorum specifies how many data-bearing voting members, or which voting members, including the primary, must be prepared to commit the index build before the primary will execute the commit. The default commit quorum is votingMembers, which means all data-bearing members. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes/ · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndexes.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndex.md
- [passage] If a data-bearing voting node becomes unreachable and the [commitQuorum](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createindexes.md#std-label-createIndexes-cmd-commitQuorum) is set to the default `votingMembers`, index builds can hang until that node comes back online. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes.md#concurrency · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build, votingMembers · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md
- [passage] The commit quorum specifies how many data-bearing voting members, or which voting members, including the primary, must be prepared to commit a [simultaneous index build](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#std-label-index-operations-simultaneous-build) before the primary will execute the commit. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes.md#commit-quorum-contrasted-with-write-concern · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setIndexCommitQuorum.md
- [passage] By default, index builds use a commit quorum of "votingMembers", or all data-bearing voting members. To start an index build with a non-default commit quorum, specify the commitQuorum parameter to createIndexes or its shell helpers db.collection.createIndex() and db.collection.createIndexes(). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build
- [passage] Index builds on a replica set or sharded cluster build simultaneously across all data-bearing replica set members. The primary requires a minimum number of data-bearing voting members (that is, commit quorum), including itself, that must complete the build before marking the index as ready for use. A "voting" member is any replica set member where [`members[n].votes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/replica-configuration.md#mongodb-rsconf-rsconf.members-n-.votes) is greater than `0`. See [Index Builds in Replicated Environments](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#std-label-index-operations-replicated-build) for more information. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build, members[n].votes · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/
- [passage] Issuing [`setIndexCommitQuorum`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setindexcommitquorum.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setIndexCommitQuorum) has no effect on index builds started with [commitQuorum](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createindexes.md#std-label-createIndexes-cmd-commitQuorum) of `0`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setIndexCommitQuorum.md#behavior · keywords: commit quorum, index, index build, setIndexCommitQuorum
- [fact] A rolling index build hides and sets priority 0 on one secondary at a time, restarts it as a standalone (no replSetName, different port, disableLogicalSessionCacheRefresh=true), runs createIndex, restarts it as a member, waits for catch-up and unhides it. After all secondaries, rs.stepDown() the primary and repeat on the former primary. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v6.3/tutorial/build-indexes-on-replica-sets · keywords: hidden index, index, index build, Index Build Strategies
- [passage] This example creates multiple indexes with the same key pattern and different `sparse` options: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique.md#unique-and-sparse-index-creation · keywords: index, index build, unique index, sparse · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md
- [fact] Heavy write load on the target collection reduces write performance and lengthens the build; MongoDB recommends a maintenance window with reduced writes. Unique-index duplicates are only detected at the end of the build, so validate data first or stop non-compliant writers. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md · keywords: index, index build, unique index, Index Build Strategies
- [fact] Bulk inserts of random data (for example hashed indexes) create random index entries. Once each insert touches a different index entry, the index no longer fits in cache, WiredTiger cache eviction and replacement rate rises, and insert performance drops. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/faq/indexes.md · keywords: hashed index, index, index overhead, Index Storage and RAM Fit and Write-Path Overhead
- [passage] Wildcard text indexes are distinct from [wildcard indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard.md#std-label-wildcard-index-core). Wildcard text indexes support queries that use the [`$text`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/text.md#mongodb-query-op.-text) operator, while wildcard indexes do not. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text/create-wildcard-text-index.md#about-this-task · keywords: index, text index, wildcard index, $text · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard.md
- [passage] The wildcard text index supports `$text` queries on all fields in the collection. Consider the following queries: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text/create-wildcard-text-index.md#results · keywords: index, text index, wildcard index, $text
- [passage] - [Drop unused, redundant, and hidden indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/drop-indexes.md#std-label-pa-drop-index) to improve write performance and free storage space. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/analyze-slow-queries.md#best-practices-for-query-performance · keywords: dropIndex, hidden index, index
- [passage] If an index specified to [`db.collection.dropIndex()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropindex.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.dropIndex) is still building, [`db.collection.dropIndex()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropindex.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.dropIndex) attempts to stop the in-progress build. Stopping an index build has the same effect as dropping the built index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropIndex.md#stop-in-progress-index-builds · keywords: dropIndex, index, index build, db.collection.dropIndex() · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/dropIndexes.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropIndexes.md
- [passage] - Hidden indexes are updated upon write operations to the collection and continue to consume disk space and memory. - [passage] Hidden indexes are updated upon write operations to the collection and continue to consume disk space and memory. As such, they are included in various statistics operations, such as db.collection.stats() and $indexStats. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden/ · keywords: collStats, hidden index, index
- [fact] Hiding an index does not reduce write cost or storage. Hidden indexes are updated on every write and keep consuming disk space and memory, and they still count in db.collection.stats() and $indexStats. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden/ · keywords: collStats, hidden index, index, Hidden Indexes
- [passage] The total uncompressed size in memory of all records in a collection. - [statement] Rolling index builds driven by Atlas, Cloud Manager and Ops Manager (affected MongoDB 4.2.19+, 4.4.13+, 5.0.6+, 6.0.0+; agent 11.13.0.7438-1 to 12.4.0.7702-1) could create indexes with log=(enabled=true), so after a replication rollback or primary crash the indexes were not rolled back with the documents, giving missing or extra entries and wrong query results. - [fact] During the build, writes to the collection are recorded as keys in a temporary side-writes table that is drained FIFO. A shared S lock (blocks writes) and then a final X lock are held only while the last records drain and the index is committed. Key-generation errors go to a constraint-violation table checked at the end. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md · keywords: index, index build, Index Build Strategies

- [passage] - Wildcard indexes omit the `_id` field by default. To include the `_id` field in the wildcard index, you must explicitly include it in the `wildcardProjection` document: ```javascript { "wildcardProjection": { "_id": 1, "<field>": 0|1 } } ``` All of the statements in the `wildcardProjection` document must be either inclusion or exclusion statements. You can also include the `_id` field with exclusion statements. This is the only exception to the rule. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes.md#wildcard-indexes · keywords: index, wildcard index, _id, wildcardProjection,  All of the statements in the

- [fact] Compound wildcard indexes were introduced in MongoDB 7.0. They hold one wildcard term plus one or more regular terms, e.g. { tenantId: 1, "customFields.$**": 1 } or { Region: 1, "Attributes.$**": 1 }, and target the attribute pattern so one index serves many dynamic sub-field queries. — https://mongodb.com/docs/v7.0/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/index-wildcard-compound · keywords: index, wildcard index, Wildcard and Compound Wildcard Indexes
- [fact] A wildcard index supports only one query predicate field per query; other predicates are resolved without it and unsupported ones show in rejectedPlans in explain output. In a compound wildcard index the wildcard term supports one predicate while the regular terms can support the rest. The planner may reuse the same wildcard index for each independent $or argument. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/upcoming/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/reference/restrictions/ · keywords: index, wildcard index, Wildcard and Compound Wildcard Indexes
- [fact] A wildcard index can satisfy a sort only if the planner picks it for the predicate, the sort names only the predicate field, and that field is never an array. A covered query additionally needs exactly one wildcard-covered predicate field and a projection that excludes _id and includes only that field. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/upcoming/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/reference/restrictions/ · keywords: index, wildcard index, Wildcard and Compound Wildcard Indexes
- [statement] No benchmark or measured numbers for wildcard or compound wildcard index performance appeared in any source read; vendor and blog claims of efficiency ("efficiently and easily", "fewer system resources") are unquantified. — https://mongodb.com/blog/post/query-enhancement-mongodb-7-0 · keywords: index, wildcard index, Wildcard and Compound Wildcard Indexes
- [fact] If a write modifies an indexed field, MongoDB updates all indexes that have that field as a key, so write-heavy applications can see index maintenance affect performance. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/faq/indexes.md · keywords: index, index overhead, Index Storage and RAM Fit and Write-Path Overhead
- [fact] Every insert adds entries to all indexes, every delete removes entries from all indexes, and an update that changes an indexed field removes the old entry and adds a new one in each affected index. — https://www.netdata.cloud/guides/mongodb/mongodb-unused-indexes/ · keywords: index, index overhead, Index Storage and RAM Fit and Write-Path Overhead
- [statement] For a bulk load, creating the index after the insert sorts data in memory and performs an ordered insert on all indexes, which the FAQ presents as the remedy for random-insert slowdown. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/faq/indexes.md · keywords: index, index overhead, Index Storage and RAM Fit and Write-Path Overhead
- [fact] Indexes in the WiredTiger internal cache use a different representation than on disk but still benefit from index prefix compression, which deduplicates common prefixes and reduces RAM use. Prefix compression is the default for all indexes and can be disabled via storage.wiredTiger.indexConfig.prefixCompression. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/wiredtiger/ · keywords: index, index overhead, Index Storage and RAM Fit and Write-Path Overhead
- [statement] Index pages compete with documents for WiredTiger cache. A large unused index leaves less cache for active data, and if eviction threads fall behind, application threads perform eviction themselves and add latency. — https://www.netdata.cloud/guides/mongodb/mongodb-unused-indexes/ · keywords: index, index overhead, Index Storage and RAM Fit and Write-Path Overhead
- [statement] Dropping an unused index takes an exclusive collection lock and can stall concurrent writes; run it in a quiet window and watch globalLock.currentQueue and opLatencies.writes before and after. — https://www.netdata.cloud/guides/mongodb/mongodb-unused-indexes/ · keywords: index, index overhead, Index Storage and RAM Fit and Write-Path Overhead

- [passage] Previous versions of MongoDB supported building indexes either in the foreground or background. Foreground index builds were fast and produced more efficient index data structures, but required blocking all read-write access to the parent database of the collection being indexed for the duration of the build.
